raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

On the AMD MI350X disaggregated-inference cluster, the `vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`
image ships an AINIC/ionic userspace provider that the hosts' ionic kernel module
rejects outright. `libibverbs` refuses every NIC at enumeration time with below error:

```
libibverbs: Warning: Driver ionic does not support the kernel ABI of 4 (supports 1 to 1) for device /sys/class/infiniband/ionic_0 [.. ionic_1 .. ionic_7]
```

**Reference**: All of the AMD DI CI fails with the same error. 
https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-distributed-inference-ci/builds/71/list

## Fix
Add `swap_ainic_userspace.sh`, which replaces the image's ionic userspace
(`libionic1`, `libionic-dev`, `ionic-common`) with a pinned `repo.radeon.com`
channel. It resolves exact package versions from the channel's `Packages` index
rather than hardcoding them (channel names and package versions do not track each
other), then `apt-mark hold`s them so a later upgrade cannot walk them forward.
Only userspace is touched; kernel modules and NIC firmware live on the host.
`run_xPyD_disagg.slurm` applies the swap in a root container before serving, then
`docker commit`s the result and serves the job from that image. The swap is done
ahead of launch rather than inside the serving container because:
- the serving container runs as the calling user (`--user $(id -u):$(id -g)`), so
  `apt` cannot run in it, and running it as root would leave root-owned artifacts
  on shared NFS;
- the ionic mount paths are read-only bind mounts in the serving container, and
  `apt` cannot replace a bind-mount target;
- the swap purges `libionic1` first, so there is a window with no usable provider,
  which must not overlap a process that is about to call into ibverbs.
The committed tag is keyed on the source image ID, so a moving tag such as
`:nightly` rebuilds automatically instead of silently serving a swap baked on top
of an older pull. Repeat runs on the same node reuse it.
## Knobs
| Variable | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AINIC_SWAP_CHANNEL` | `1.117.3-hydra` | Channel to install. `none` disables the swap and serves the image's own provider. |
| `SKIP_IONIC_MOUNTS` | `0` | `1` skips the host ionic bind-mounts. |
The two compose: the bake deliberately runs without the mounts so `apt` can write
those paths, and the mounts are layered back on at serve time unless skipped.

## Test plan
DeepSeek-V3, TP 1P1D (`WIDE_EP_MODE=0 xP=1 yD=1`), 2x MI350X nodes, gsm8k
accuracy gate, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`:
| Config | Devices seen | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mounts only (pre-change baseline) | 8 | PASS `exact_match=0.9424` |
| No mounts, no swap | **0** | **FAIL** — 16 workers aborted in `RdmaManager` |
| Swap, no mounts | 8 | PASS `exact_match=0.9424` |
| Swap + mounts | 8 | PASS `exact_match=0.9484` |
| Swap, no mounts (this branch on a clean main) | 8 | PASS `exact_match=0.9477` |
The swapped image was also verified directly: packages installed and held, and
`ibv_get_device_list()` returning all 8 devices (`ionic_0`..`ionic_7`) where the
unmodified image returned 0.

## Additional Notes 
The swap defaults to **on** so this cluster's CI is correct without extra
configuration. On a cluster whose image provider already matches its kernel
module, set `AINIC_SWAP_CHANNEL=none`. It also requires the compute nodes to
reach `repo.radeon.com`.

@@ -71,6 +71,10 @@ export IMAGE MODEL_NAME WIDE_EP_MODE xP yD GPUS_PER_NODE RUN_AFTER_HEALTH HEALTH
 export SHARED_MOUNT LOG_ROOT DRY_RUN MORIIO_READ_MODE
 export ROUTER_TYPE ROUTER_PORT VLLM_ROUTER_IMAGE
 
+# ionic/AINIC RoCE userspace: leave the image's own provider in place, and/or bake
+# a specific repo.radeon.com channel into the run image.
+export SKIP_IONIC_MOUNTS AINIC_SWAP_CHANNEL
+
 # Model selection.
 [[ -n "${MODEL_NAME:-}" ]] && export MODEL_NAME
 [[ -n "${MODEL_DIR:-}" ]] && export MODEL_DIR

@@ -24,6 +24,16 @@ RUN_AFTER_HEALTH="${RUN_AFTER_HEALTH:-accuracy}"   # bench | accuracy
 DRY_RUN="${DRY_RUN:-0}"
 MORIIO_READ_MODE="${MORIIO_READ_MODE:-0}"   # 0 -> prefill writes (default); 1 -> decode reads KV (read_mode)
 
+# ---- ionic / AINIC RoCE userspace -------------------------------------------
+# The nightly images ship a provider that this cluster's ionic kernel module
+# rejects outright ("does not support the kernel ABI of 4"), which leaves MoRI
+# with zero devices, so default to the channel that matches the module. Set
+# AINIC_SWAP_CHANNEL=none to serve the image's own provider unchanged; an empty
+# value is treated as unset, so `none` is the way to opt out.
+SKIP_IONIC_MOUNTS="${SKIP_IONIC_MOUNTS:-0}"
+AINIC_SWAP_CHANNEL="${AINIC_SWAP_CHANNEL:-1.117.3-hydra}"
+[ "$AINIC_SWAP_CHANNEL" = "none" ] && AINIC_SWAP_CHANNEL=""
+
 # ---- router / gateway (host-side; also forwarded into the container) --------
 # vllm-router -> external `vllm/vllm-router` container started on the rank-0 node (default)
 # proxy       -> in-container MoRIIO proxy (no extra container)
@@ -385,15 +395,21 @@ run_node_container() {
     # container IF present: the image ships an ABI-incompatible copy and the NICs
     # are invisible without the host libs. Each entry is added only when the host
     # file exists, so this is a no-op on non-ionic (e.g. mlx5) clusters.
+    #
+    # SKIP_IONIC_MOUNTS=1 leaves the image's own ionic userspace in place
     local IONIC_MOUNTS=()
     local host_ionic
-    host_ionic=$(readlink -f /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libionic.so.1 2>/dev/null || true)
-    [ -n "$host_ionic" ] && IONIC_MOUNTS+=(-v "$host_ionic:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libionic.so.1:ro")
-    [ -f /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libibverbs/libionic-rdmav34.so ] && \
-        IONIC_MOUNTS+=(-v "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libibverbs/libionic-rdmav34.so:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libibverbs/libionic-rdmav34.so:ro")
-    [ -f /etc/libibverbs.d/ionic.driver ] && \
-        IONIC_MOUNTS+=(-v "/etc/libibverbs.d/ionic.driver:/etc/libibverbs.d/ionic.driver:ro")
-    echo "Rank $rank ionic mounts: ${IONIC_MOUNTS[*]:-<none>}"
+    if [ "$SKIP_IONIC_MOUNTS" = "1" ]; then
+        echo "Rank $rank ionic mounts: <skipped: SKIP_IONIC_MOUNTS=1>"
+    else
+        host_ionic=$(readlink -f /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libionic.so.1 2>/dev/null || true)
+        [ -n "$host_ionic" ] && IONIC_MOUNTS+=(-v "$host_ionic:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libionic.so.1:ro")
+        [ -f /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libibverbs/libionic-rdmav34.so ] && \
+            IONIC_MOUNTS+=(-v "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libibverbs/libionic-rdmav34.so:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libibverbs/libionic-rdmav34.so:ro")
+        [ -f /etc/libibverbs.d/ionic.driver ] && \
+            IONIC_MOUNTS+=(-v "/etc/libibverbs.d/ionic.driver:/etc/libibverbs.d/ionic.driver:ro")
+        echo "Rank $rank ionic mounts: ${IONIC_MOUNTS[*]:-<none>}"
+    fi
 
     # Pull latest container.
     if [ "$DRY_RUN" != "1" ]; then
@@ -405,6 +421,53 @@ run_node_container() {
         fi
     fi
 
+    # Replace the image's ionic RoCE userspace with another repo.radeon.com
+    # channel. An image whose provider is rejected by libibverbs against the host
+    # kernel module ("Driver ionic does not support the kernel ABI of N") exposes
+    # no devices at all, so MoRI enumerates zero of them and every worker aborts on
+    # `availDevices.size() > 0' in RdmaManager. The swap needs apt as root, but the
+    # serving container runs as the calling user, so bake a committed image here
+    # and serve from that instead.
+    #
+    # This composes with the ionic mounts above: the bake deliberately runs without
+    # them so apt can write those paths, and they are layered back on at serve time
+    # unless SKIP_IONIC_MOUNTS=1.
+    RUN_IMAGE="$IMAGE"
+    if [ -n "$AINIC_SWAP_CHANNEL" ] && [ "$DRY_RUN" != "1" ]; then
+        local src_id ainic_tag build_cont swap_rc
+        src_id=$(docker image inspect -f '{{.Id}}' "$IMAGE" 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f2 | cut -c1-12)
+        # Key the tag on the source image id so a moving tag (e.g. :nightly) cannot
+        # silently serve a swap baked on top of an older pull.
+        ainic_tag="vllm-disagg-ainic:${AINIC_SWAP_CHANNEL}-${src_id:-unknown}"
+        if docker image inspect "$ainic_tag" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+            echo "Rank $rank ainic swap: reusing $ainic_tag"
+        else
+            echo "Rank $rank ainic swap: building $ainic_tag from $IMAGE"
+            build_cont="ainic-swap-${SLURM_JOB_ID:-0}-${rank}"
+            docker stop -t 30 "$build_cont" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+            docker rm "$build_cont" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+            if docker run --name "$build_cont" --user 0:0 --network host \
+                    -v "$DISAGG_SCRIPTS_DIR":"$CONTAINER_SCRIPTS":ro \
+                    --entrypoint /bin/bash "$IMAGE" \
+                    -c "bash $CONTAINER_SCRIPTS/swap_ainic_userspace.sh $AINIC_SWAP_CHANNEL" \
+               && docker commit "$build_cont" "$ainic_tag" >/dev/null; then
+                echo "Rank $rank ainic swap: committed $ainic_tag"
+                swap_rc=0
+            else
+                echo "ERROR: rank $rank ainic swap to $AINIC_SWAP_CHANNEL failed on $(hostname)" >&2
+                swap_rc=1
+            fi
+            # Reached on both paths so a failed bake cannot leave the name behind
+            # and block the next attempt. The container has already exited by now,
+            # so the stop is a no-op that keeps teardown uniform with the rest of
+            # the script.
+            docker stop -t 30 "$build_cont" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+            docker rm "$build_cont" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+            [ "$swap_rc" = "0" ] || return 1
+        fi
+        RUN_IMAGE="$ainic_tag"
+    fi
+
     # Start the external vLLM router as a SEPARATE container on the rank-0 node.
     if [ "$ROUTER_TYPE" = "vllm-router" ] && [ "$rank" = "0" ] && [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
         echo "DRY_RUN: would start vllm-router on $(hostname): $VLLM_ROUTER_IMAGE (discovery :$PROXY_PING_PORT, port :$ROUTER_PORT, policy $ROUTER_POLICY, dp_local=$ROUTER_DP_LOCAL)"
@@ -478,7 +541,7 @@ run_node_container() {
         -e GATEWAY_PORT="$GATEWAY_PORT" \
         --name "$DOCKER_CONT_NAME" \
         --entrypoint /bin/bash \
-        "$IMAGE" -c "bash $CONTAINER_SCRIPTS/vllm_disagg.sh node" \
+        "$RUN_IMAGE" -c "bash $CONTAINER_SCRIPTS/vllm_disagg.sh node" \
       2>&1 | tee "$LOG_PATH/main_NODE${rank}.log"
     local node_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}   # docker run exit code (not tee), for rank-0 pass/fail
     # Stop the external router (rank-0 node) once the main container returns.

@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Swap the AINIC/ionic *userspace* RoCE provider inside a vllm-openai-rocm
+# container to a different repo.radeon.com channel.
+#
+# Only libionic1 / libionic-dev / ionic-common exist in this image. The kernel
+# modules (ionic-dkms and required libraries) and the NIC firmware live on the host and are
+# NOT touched here.
+#
+#   ./swap_ainic_userspace.sh --list
+#   ./swap_ainic_userspace.sh 1.117.5-a-56
+#   ./swap_ainic_userspace.sh 1.117.5-a-56 --dry-run
+#
+set -euo pipefail
+
+REPO=https://repo.radeon.com/amdainic/pensando/ubuntu
+PKGS=(libionic-dev libionic1 ionic-common)
+DRY=0
+
+die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+[[ "${1:-}" == "--list" ]] && {
+    curl -fsS "$REPO/" | grep -oP '(?<=href=")[0-9][^"]*(?=/")' | sort -V
+    exit 0
+}
+
+CHANNEL="${1:-}"
+[[ -n "$CHANNEL" ]] || die "usage: $0 <channel|--list> [--dry-run]"
+[[ "${2:-}" == "--dry-run" ]] && DRY=1
+
+[[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "must run as root inside the container"
+
+. /etc/os-release
+CODENAME="${VERSION_CODENAME:?cannot determine ubuntu codename}"
+
+echo "==> current state"
+dpkg-query -W -f='    ${Package} ${Version}\n' "${PKGS[@]}" 2>/dev/null || echo "    (none installed)"
+
+# Resolve exact versions from the target channel rather than hardcoding them:
+# the channel name and the package versions do not track each other.
+echo "==> resolving ${CHANNEL} (${CODENAME})"
+INDEX=$(curl -fsS "$REPO/$CHANNEL/dists/$CODENAME/main/binary-amd64/Packages") \
+    || die "no such channel/codename: $CHANNEL/$CODENAME"
+
+declare -a PINS=()
+for p in "${PKGS[@]}"; do
+    v=$(awk -v P="$p" '$1=="Package:"&&$2==P{f=1;next} f&&$1=="Version:"{print $2;exit}' <<<"$INDEX")
+    [[ -n "$v" ]] || die "$p not present in channel $CHANNEL"
+    echo "    $p=$v"
+    PINS+=("$p=$v")
+done
+
+if [[ $DRY -eq 1 ]]; then echo "==> dry run, stopping"; exit 0; fi
+
+# Purging libionic1 removes /etc/libibverbs.d/ionic.driver, so there is no
+# usable RoCE provider between here and the install below. Do not run this
+# while a job is holding QPs on the device.
+echo "==> purging existing"
+apt-mark unhold "${PKGS[@]}" 2>/dev/null || true
+apt-get purge -y "${PKGS[@]}" 2>/dev/null || true
+
+echo "==> pointing apt at ${CHANNEL}"
+install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings
+[[ -f /etc/apt/keyrings/amdainic.gpg ]] || \
+    curl -fsSL https://repo.radeon.com/rocm/rocm.gpg.key | gpg --dearmor > /etc/apt/keyrings/amdainic.gpg
+echo "deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/amdainic.gpg] $REPO/$CHANNEL $CODENAME main" \
+    > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/amdainic.list
+
+# Update only this list. libc6/libibverbs1 are already installed, so the
+# other lists (purged at image build time) are not needed.
+APT_ONLY=(-o Dir::Etc::sourcelist=/etc/apt/sources.list.d/amdainic.list
+          -o Dir::Etc::sourceparts=/dev/null)
+apt-get "${APT_ONLY[@]}" update
+
+echo "==> installing"
+apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends --allow-downgrades "${PINS[@]}"
+
+# Without the hold, any later apt upgrade silently walks this back forward.
+apt-mark hold "${PKGS[@]}"
+ldconfig
+
+echo "==> verify"
+dpkg-query -W -f='    ${Package} ${Version}\n' "${PKGS[@]}"
+ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libionic.so.1 /etc/libibverbs.d/ionic.driver
+command -v ibv_devinfo >/dev/null && ibv_devinfo 2>&1 | head -20 || true
+
